words.technical: Gold sits at the bottom of its one-year range, and all four trend windows are negative, the shorter three firmly, so the metal is in a clear downtrend rather than a pause. The week's drop is large against gold's normal daily swings.
words.macro: Futures markets priced a December Fed rate hike at 100% odds. Central banks bought a net 321 tonnes of gold in the third quarter, up 42% from a year earlier.
words.long_term: Official-sector buying remains the structural support under gold, but a rising-rate regime raises the opportunity cost of holding it, and that tension is what the trend is currently resolving.

eoy_scenarios.central: Gold drifts in a wide, choppy range as rate-hike pricing and central-bank buying roughly offset each other through year-end.
eoy_scenarios.upside: A softer inflation print or a hawkish repricing that fades lets the dollar retreat, and renewed official-sector buying pulls gold back above the central band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: A firm December hike with guidance for more keeps the dollar bid and real returns attractive, pushing gold through the lower edge of the central band.

words.technical: Silver is at the very bottom of its one-year range after a steeper weekly drop than gold, and its short and medium trend windows are strongly negative. Silver also moves more than gold on a typical day, so its weekly range is proportionally wider. Weakness is broad across the trend windows rather than a single-day shock.
words.macro: Silver tumbled below $52 an ounce on 10 November. US core inflation stayed at 0.3% for a third straight month, above the 0.2% economists expected.
words.long_term: Silver carries both a monetary and an industrial identity, so it tends to amplify gold's direction in either direction; the standing picture is a high-volatility metal that needs the rate backdrop to stop tightening before a durable base forms.

eoy_scenarios.central: Silver stays range-bound and volatile, tracking gold and the dollar with larger swings.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Easing rate-hike pricing and a gold rebound pull silver back above the central band, with industrial demand adding support.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Continued dollar strength and further hikes extend the slide below the central band, as forced selling in thin conditions adds to losses.

words.technical: Oil ended the week mid-range with almost no net trend: the shortest window is negative, the medium windows are mixed, and the longest is positive. That balance reads as a market in transition rather than one with a direction. The weekly range is wide because oil's daily swings are the largest of the seven instruments here.
words.macro: WTI fell 4.38% on 9 November to settle at $86.85 a barrel. WTI is set for a 2.9% weekly decline after dropping 13% the week before.
words.long_term: Oil's structural picture is a geopolitical risk premium set against a supply outlook that has been easing, so prices swing between the two rather than trending.

eoy_scenarios.central: Crude trades around current levels as the risk premium and softer supply balance out.
eoy_scenarios.upside: A renewed supply disruption or stalled diplomacy rebuilds the risk premium and lifts crude above the central band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Progress toward de-escalation plus continued stock builds pushes crude below the central band.

words.technical: Bitcoin had the biggest weekly drop of the seven and its shortest trend window is sharply negative, though the two longest windows are roughly flat. That pattern describes a sharp pullback inside a wider sideways year rather than a collapse of the long trend. Price sits in the lower third of its one-year range.
words.macro: Spot Bitcoin funds recorded a $284 million net outflow on 12 November, the sixth consecutive day of withdrawals. October nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000, which a market report said gave the Fed no reason to pause. Bitcoin traded around $75,800 on 6 November after the October jobs report.
words.long_term: Bitcoin trades as a liquidity-sensitive risk asset, so rising policy rates and fund outflows weigh on it, while its long-run range has held for a year.

eoy_scenarios.central: Bitcoin consolidates in the lower half of its yearly range while fund flows stabilise.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Flows turn positive and rate-hike fears ease, lifting bitcoin back above the central band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Outflows continue and a hawkish December decision tightens liquidity, taking bitcoin below the central band.

words.technical: The dollar index closed the week at the top of its one-year range with positive readings across every trend window, which makes it the most consistent trend of the seven instruments. Daily volatility is the lowest of the group, so even a modest weekly gain is large relative to normal movement. A reading at the very top of the range also means the dollar is stretched and can reverse quickly.
words.macro: Traders lifted bets on a 25-basis-point December Fed rate hike to 87%, from about 70% a month earlier. The dollar index touched its highest level since April 2025 on 11 November. US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% forecast. Markets priced a 91% chance of a December hike, up from 84% a day earlier.
words.long_term: The dollar's standing picture is a widening interest-rate gap in its favour, with the policy path rather than growth doing most of the work.

eoy_scenarios.central: The dollar holds near its highs as hike pricing settles, with small moves either side.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Hotter data and more hawkish guidance extend the rate gap, and the dollar breaks above the central band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Softer inflation or a cautious policy message unwinds hike pricing, and the dollar slips below the central band.

week_summary: A hawkish rate repricing set the tone: US inflation again came in above forecasts, markets priced a December Fed rate hike as near certain, and the dollar climbed to a multi-month high. Gold and silver sold off hard into the bottom of their yearly ranges, bitcoin had the largest weekly drop, and oil slipped for a second week. US stocks still finished higher despite a sharp slide in chip names and a 10-year yield above 5%. Stances lean defensive where the trend is clearly negative and neutral where the weekly range already captures the likely move.
